analysis.investment_thesis: Aequs is a capital-intensive, loss-making contract manufacturer trading at an irrational 1,140x forward P/E with a ₹11,202 Cr market cap — failing every single SMILE criterion from size to profitability. The heavy capex story (₹395 Cr CWIP) is speculative at best when revenue actually declined from ₹965 Cr to ₹925 Cr and net losses widened to ₹102 Cr in FY25.
key_strengths: Promoter holding at 59.08% shows skin in the game
Gross margin of 56% suggests some pricing power in aerospace components
Operating in India's aerospace defense manufacturing theme — a real structural tailwind
key_risks: Market cap of ₹11,202 Cr — 10x outside Kedia's ₹1,000 Cr sweet spot, pricing in a future that may never arrive
Free cash flow deeply negative and worsening: -₹76 Cr → -₹175 Cr → -₹239 Cr over 3 years, with D/E at 1.08x above my 0.4x threshold
Revenue growth has stalled (₹965 Cr → ₹925 Cr in FY25) while the company keeps burning cash on capex — execution not visible
red_flags: Forward P/E of 1,140x — pure speculation, not investing
Operating margin negative at -1.84%; ROE deeply negative at -11.2%
Net losses widened back to ₹102 Cr in FY25 after improvement to ₹14 Cr in FY24 — not a turnaround
Borrowings jumped from ₹664 Cr to ₹785 Cr while generating no returns
Diversified across aerospace, toys, cookware, logistics — no focused niche moat
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aequs violates every principle of the SMILE framework. At ₹11,202 Cr market cap, it is 10x too large for my universe. The valuation is simply divorced from reality — EV/EBITDA of 288x and a forward P/E of 1,140x mean the market is paying for a dream, not a business. Operating margins are negative (-1.84%), ROCE is barely 1%, and free cash flow has deteriorated every single year to -₹239 Cr in FY25. Debt at 1.08x equity funds this capex-heavy model, adding financial risk to operational risk. Revenue even shrank in FY25 — there is no demonstrated growth to justify any premium, let alone this one.

The only silver lining is that ₹395 Cr of CWIP signals heavy capacity being built, and the 56% gross margin hints the underlying aerospace business has merit — but that story needs 3-5 years of execution before it becomes investable. I want to buy a company that has already proven the business model at small scale and is ready to scale nationally, not one still figuring out if it can make money. Aequs is a venture bet dressed up as a listed equity. Let it prove profitability, reduce debt, and come down to a ₹500-1,000 Cr market cap through dilution or correction before it enters my conversation.
